PullRequest.Title: chat: check nested subagent calls against the caller's allowlist
PullRequest.Body: Fixes #335257 ## Problem Custom agents can limit which subagents they call with the `agents:` frontmatter list. #331442 (fixing #331002) enforced that list in `runSubagent`, but it always resolved the "current agent" from `model.getRequests().at(-1)`. That is the top-level request, because subagent requests reuse the session and are never added to the chat model. So in a chain A → B → C, B's call to C was checked against **A's** list and rejected with `Requested agent 'C' is not allowed by the current agent.` Any nested call two or more levels deep failed. Enabling `chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents` doesn't help, since it only limits nesting depth. ## Fix - **Identify the caller.** Tool invocation tokens now carry the id of the request they were issued for (`IToolInvocationContext.requestId`, set in `ChatAgentRequest.to`). The token is opaque to extensions (`ChatParticipantToolToken` is `never`) and is passed back unchanged on every `vscode.lm.invokeTool` call, so each subagent's tool calls carry its own request id. `prepareToolInvocation` receives it as `IToolInvocationPreparationContext.invocationRequestId`. There are no API changes. - **Track running subagents.** `RunSubagentTool` keeps a map of the subagents it started, keyed by their request id (the `callId` of the `runSubagent` call that started them). An entry is added right before `invokeAgent` and removed in the same `finally` that decrements the nesting depth. - **Validate against the caller.** Both `prepareToolInvocation` and `invoke` use the calling subagent's instructions and allowlist. Calls made in the top-level request fall back to the previous behavior. - **Why the request id.** The caller is identified by request id rather than `subAgentInvocationId`. That id comes from the model's tool call id, which is not guaranteed to be unique (some models reuse tool call ids), so parallel subagents could resolve to the wrong caller. Unchanged from #331442: top-level enforcement in both `prepareToolInvocation` and `invoke`, each subagent carrying its own `agents:` list, and passing the allowlist to automatic instruction collection. ### Behavior change for nested calls without `agentName` When a nested subagent calls `runSubagent` without `agentName`, the new subagent is now a copy of the **calling subagent**: its instructions, allowlist, model, tools and frontmatter hooks. Previously it silently became a copy of the top-level agent. That let a subagent step outside its own allowlist, and with only the allowlist fixed, the copy would have run on a model that is neither the subagent's own nor the Auto default from #333663. An explicit `model` still goes through the usual checks. ## Tests 7 new tests, all of which fail without the fix: - `runSubagentTool.test.ts`: - 3 and 4 levels of nesting. - The caller's allowlist decides, not the top-level agent's. - Parallel subagents started by tool calls with the same id each resolve their own caller. - What a copy inherits: instructions, allowlist, model, tools and hooks. - A finished or failed subagent is no longer treated as the caller. - `languageModelToolsService.test.ts`: the invocation request id reaches `prepareToolInvocation`. - `extHostTypeConverter.test.ts`: the tool invocation token carries the request id. The 3 suites (205 tests) pass, as do the broader chat tools (455), API chat and language model (87), and chat model and service (457) tests. `npm run typecheck-client` and ESLint are clean. The change was reviewed iteratively with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5. Their findings are addressed: colliding tool call ids, copies running on the wrong model, and copies losing hooks. Both final passes found no significant issues. ## Manual validation in Code OSS Agents: Coordinator (`agents: [Worker]`) → Worker (`agents: [Specialist]`) → Specialist, plus a Forbidden agent, with `chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents` enabled. | Scenario | Result | |---|---| | Without the fix: Coordinator → Worker → Specialist | ❌ `Requested agent 'Specialist' is not allowed by the current agent.` (the bug reproduces) | | With the fix: same chain | ✅ `SPECIALIST_OK`, 3 nested levels | | Worker → Forbidden | ✅ rejected; Forbidden never ran | | Coordinator → Forbidden or Specialist directly (the #331002 check) | ✅ rejected | | Worker copies itself (no `agentName`) → Specialist, 4 levels | ✅ the copy runs as Worker; `SPECIALIST_OK` | | Final build smoke test with a different model | ✅ | ## Not changed - A copy of the **top-level** agent (no `agentName` and no calling subagent) still doesn't get that agent's frontmatter hooks. That was already the case before this change, so it's left for a follow-up. - A copy reports its caller's model selection source in the `chat.subagentModelSelection` telemetry event. ## Functional Subagents

Scenarios.Scenario: An extension-host chat agent invokes a language-model tool from a top-level or subagent request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The chat request is converted to an extension API request, the extension invokes a tool, and the existing extension-host IPC carries the tool invocation DTO back to the workbench before tool preparation/execution can proceed. The diff only adds the originating requestId to the existing token and DTO; it adds no await or boundary call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing tool invocation DTO between the extension host and workbench
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing IPC round trip per tool invocation; the diff adds one string field to that payload and does not add a round trip.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same tool invocation crossed IPC with sessionResource and optional workingDirectory but without requestId.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing IPC is on the tool invocation critical path, but the incremental serialization/allocation is constant-sized.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One short request identifier per tool invocation. Cost scales linearly with the number of tool calls already made by the agent, with constant additional payload per call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged; tool calls retain the model/tool service's existing scheduling. The new field introduces no queue, mutex, limiter, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lookup is added on this propagation path. Cold and warm behavior differ only in pre-existing agent/model/tool caches; the requestId is directly copied.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the conversion, opaque token propagation, DTO construction, and preparation context were traced end to end.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Request IDs are expected to be short call identifiers; exact serialized-byte overhead varies by identifier length but remains one field per existing call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds only constant payload and property-copy work to an existing IPC call.

Scenarios.Scenario: A running named subagent invokes another named subagent, including parallel sibling subagents
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The nested runSubagent call performs constant-time caller lookup and allowlist validation, resolves the requested agent/model, collects existing instructions/hooks, then invokes the default agent. Successful nested agent execution is on the parent tool call's critical path; this PR intentionally restores that workflow where the old caller lookup rejected valid chains.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the extension-host chat agent for each accepted nested subagent request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing agent invocation per accepted runSubagent call, with chain depth capped at 5; parallel siblings retain model-selected cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary existed for runSubagent. In valid B-to-C chains the buggy top-level allowlist could reject the call before this boundary; the diff intentionally allows the requested product workflow to execute.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each accepted nested agent must complete before its runSubagent tool result completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The invoked Copilot/default agent performs its normal language-model request(s)
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per accepted subagent and its bounded tool-calling loop; the PR does not change loop limits or request scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent model requests already occurred for accepted runSubagent calls; invalid caller resolution prevented some intended nested calls from reaching them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model responses dominate nested-agent latency and are required for the restored nested workflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Nested chain depth is bounded by RUN_SUBAGENT_MAX_NESTING_DEPTH=5 per session. Parallel cardinality is the number of model-issued sibling runSubagent calls; each active request contributes one map entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sibling subagents may run concurrently as before. The new map neither serializes nor increases sibling concurrency; entries are keyed per request so caller resolution remains constant-time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model preparation continues to use the pre-existing _resolvedModels per-tool-call cache. The new _runningSubagents state is active-lifetime state rather than a cache and is deleted in the invokeAgent finally block on success, failure, or cancellation settlement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed map lifetime, nested caller lookup, depth cap, and invokeAgent call path were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact sibling concurrency and model latency depend on generated tool calls and provider response times, but map cardinality and nesting bounds are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Additional work only occurs when a formerly broken but allowed nested workflow now proceeds; bookkeeping is O(active subagents), constant-time per call, and cleaned deterministically.

Scenarios.Scenario: A nested runSubagent call omits agentName and copies the calling subagent's model, tools, instructions, and hooks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The call looks up the running caller, shallow-copies its tool enablement map because the child mutates depth/tool restrictions, reuses the already-resolved model, merges global and agent hooks, and invokes the same agent. Model and agent invocation boundaries already existed for no-name copies.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the extension-host agent for the copied subagent
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing invocation per no-name runSubagent call; depth capped at 5.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A no-name call already invoked an agent, but incorrectly copied top-level rather than calling-subagent configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required and unchanged for the child subagent to execute.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute inherited frontmatter hook commands such as SubagentStop/PreToolUse
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serial subprocess per configured command for each applicable hook event in the copied subagent; nesting is capped at 5, while Pre/PostToolUse follows that subagent's existing tool-call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No-name nested copies omitted the calling subagent's frontmatter hooks, so those configured commands did not run for the copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configured hooks are awaited and can add their configured command duration to the child agent's path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform the copied agent's normal model request(s)
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per copied subagent/tool loop; no additional model invocation is introduced by inheriting the correct model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The no-name child already ran a model, but could resolve a different top-level/default model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for subagent progress and unchanged in count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one shallow copy over registered tool enablement entries per copied subagent. Agent hooks scale with explicitly configured hook commands and nested depth, which is capped at 5.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Nested copies execute through the existing parent tool call; parallel top-level branches remain possible and unchanged. Hook commands are executed serially by the existing ChatHookService per hook event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The inherited resolved model bypasses repeated auto-model/custom-agent discovery on the warm nested path. The copied metadata is retained only while the child agent runs and is deleted in finally.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the shallow copy, inherited model fast path, hook merge without accumulation, max depth, and serial command executor were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tool-map size and user hook duration vary. Hook commands may be slow, but their execution is explicit configured behavior required by making the child a true copy rather than accidental repeated work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The only newly reached subprocess work is the intentional execution of explicitly configured hooks for a child that now correctly copies its caller; hooks are not duplicated or accumulated across generations, and nesting is bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all seven changed files and relevant transitive agent, IPC, model, hook, cache, concurrency, and cleanup paths. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not provide sufficient evidence of a shipped performance regression fix to record.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
